claims.text: The initial feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Under standard or non-optimized HVAF-i7 spray-distance conditions, this feedstock produces acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
Optimizing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity.
A spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm is appropriate for the HVAF-i7 nozzle.
Higher particle velocity will enhance particle impact energy.
Enhanced impact energy will improve splat formation.
Enhanced impact energy and improved splat formation will increase deposition efficiency.
Higher particle velocity will promote improved in-flight melting of the feedstock particles.
Improved particle melting and substrate impact will produce thicker and more adherent coatings.
The proposed velocity increase will enable thicker coating builds without additional oxidation.
The optimized spray distance will significantly increase coating thickness relative to the non-optimized HVAF-i7 baseline.
The optimized coating will retain acceptable as-sprayed oxidation and adhesion for high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective when coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention will remain effective during high-temperature thermal-barrier usage.
Effects of optimized spray distance observed for conventional MCrAlY may not translate directly to FeCoNiCrAl processed with HVAF-i7 because of material- and process-specific behavior.
